physical_harm: No injury on the private parts of the prosecutrix, only a minor abrasion on the right side neck below jaw
number_of_offences: Two offences/counts charged, both upheld by the trial court and High Court, but overturned by the Supreme Court
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court did not accept the prosecution's version of the case, noting contradictions in the prosecutrix's statement, inconsistencies in the eye-witness accounts, and the FSL report not correlating with the alleged version.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, including the prosecutrix, as unreliable, noting contradictions in her statements, variations in her version of events, and the lack of support from her niece and nephew, who were the eye-witnesses.
trial_duration: Offence: 15.08.2001; Trial judgment: 27.01.2009; High Court decision: 27.01.2009; Supreme Court decision: 07.08.2012
legal_representation: Ashok K. Srivastava, Saurabh Trivedi, Shiv Sagar Tiwari for the Appellant; Mohan Jain, ASG, D.K. Thakur, P.K. Dey, Karthik Ashok, Shubham, Aggarwal, A.K. Sharma, B.V. Bairam Das, Anil Katiyar for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR lodged at 14.20 hours on 16.08.2001; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and sentence imposed; High Court: Upheld conviction and sentence; Supreme Court: Acquitted, set aside trial court and High Court judgments
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused-appellants committed gang rape on the prosecutrix on 15.08.2001 at 1.30 a.m., based on the FIR and the evidence of the prosecutrix, her niece and nephew, and the FSL report. They contended that the evidence was sufficient to sustain the conviction and sentence under Section 376(2)(g) of the IPC.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution's case was based on a solitary version of the prosecutrix, which was inconsistent with the FIR, cross-examination, and the evidence of the eye-witnesses. They also pointed out contradictions in the FSL report and the lack of corroboration, which made the prosecution's case unreliable.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the testimony of the prosecutrix alone is not sufficient to sustain a conviction for gang rape unless it is corroborated, especially when there are contradictions in her statement, inconsistencies in the evidence, and lack of supporting forensic or witness evidence.
precedent_relied_upon: Lalliram & Anr. v. State of Madhya Pradesh - 2008 (13) SCR 395 = 2008 (10) SCC 69; Krishan Kumar Malik v. State of Haryana 2011 (8) SCR 774 = 2011(7) SCC 130; State of Punjab v. Gurmit Singh & Ors. - 1996 (1) SCR 532 = 1996 (2) SCC 384; State of Himachal Pradesh v. Asha Ram 2005 (5) Suppl. SCR 280 = AIR 2006 SC 381
